title: Assessment of Stress Levels (Stress Processing and Biomarkers) during Inpatient Rehabilitation in Patients with Substance Use Disorders – A Prospective, Exploratory Analysis of Psychobiological Parameters
summary:
Stress has a strong influence on the development and course of addiction. People with substance dependence often react more strongly to stressful situations, which can lead to strong urges to use the substance and increase the risk of relapse.
This study examines how stressed patients feel during their inpatient treatment and how they cope with stress. It also investigates whether stress levels and stress-coping strategies change during the stay and whether there are differences between different groups (for example, depending on the main substance or additional mental health problems).
During treatment, several blood samples are taken and a questionnaire on stress-coping is completed. In addition, some information about personal history and current life circumstances is collected. The study follows how these values change over time in order to better understand possible connections between stress, coping, and different influencing factors.
conditions: Mental and behavioural disorders due to psychoactive substance use

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The study population includes all patients who meet the inclusion criteria and are treated at the Bezirkskrankenhaus Hochstadt during the defined data collection period (planned as a one-year cohort). Eligible participants are adults who undergo inpatient withdrawal treatment for a substance-related disorder in the clinic and who are willing to provide written informed consent to participate in the study. The substance-related disorder according to ICD-10 must be either alcohol dependence (F10.2) or stimulant use disorder (F15.1/F15.2), provided that alcohol or amphetamine/methamphetamine represents the primary substance and the main reason for inpatient withdrawal treatment.
For the alcohol group, inclusion requires a current diagnosis of F10.2, with alcohol being the primary substance and the main reason for inpatient withdrawal treatment. Additional use or dependence on other substances is permitted, except for a current stimulant use disorder (F15.1/F15.2) as the primary substance.
For the methamphetamine/amphetamine group, inclusion requires a current diagnosis of F15.1 and/or F15.2 within the stimulant category (F15), provided that methamphetamine/amphetamine is the primary substance and the main reason for inpatient treatment. Additional use or dependence on other substances is permitted, except for current alcohol dependence (F10.2) as the primary substance.
Patients with multiple substance use disorders (F19.1/F19.2) are excluded from both groups. Further prerequisites for participation are the ability to provide informed consent and a planned inpatient stay.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients with multiple substance use disorders (F19.1/F19.2), patients with a current alcohol dependence (F10.2) in the stimulant group, individuals who are unable to provide informed consent, and those who do not provide written consent to participate are excluded.
